theater: 奧龍特斯河谷與幼發拉底河上游

battle.name: 第五次敘利亞戰役
battle.theater: 奧龍特斯河谷與幼發拉底河上游
battle.brief: 前1450年，圖特摩斯三世第五次北征敘利亞，大軍沿奧龍特斯河谷推進，擊退以米坦尼為首的聯軍，再度把幼發拉底河上游的卡爾凱美什推入埃及鋒線之前。步兵以月牙形青銅短劍配圓盾近身砍殺，弓手在兩翼鋪開箭雨，車兵留作突擊破陣，是這一役的骨幹。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 交戰的兩方是埃及新王國第十八王朝與以胡里人為核心的米坦尼聯盟。埃及方面由法老圖特摩斯三世親任全軍統帥，王室近衛與弓手隊直屬國王指揮，軍隊骨架是步兵：中央為持圓盾、長柄銅斧與短矛的重裝步兵，兩翼及前鋒是數量最多的埃及弓手，另有數百輛雙輪戰車編成突擊縱隊，御者與射手同車；後方跟著牛車與驢騾隊運糧，軍中文書逐日記下宿營地與所經城鎮。聯盟方面是上美索不達米亞的胡里王國，其王自稱「大王」，以宗主身分控制敘利亞諸邦——卡脫納、圖尼普、阿勒頗、比布魯斯與西頓——以及幼發拉底河中游的卡爾凱美什、埃馬爾，並拉攏奧龍特斯河谷的沙丘游牧部族。聯軍以步兵、車兵與胡里弓手為骨幹，另有各城邦拼湊的雜色傭兵。赫梯此時仍據安納托利亞高原，巴比倫掌握青金石與錫的來源，兩者都不直接參戰，卻決定了這場戰爭物資的流向。
countriesEn: Two sides met in this war: the New Kingdom of Egypt under the Eighteenth Dynasty, and a Mitanni-led coalition built around Hurrian power. On the Egyptian side the pharaoh Thutmose III commanded the whole army in person; the royal guard and the corps of archers answered directly to him, and the backbone of the force was infantry: heavy troops in the centre carrying round shields, long-handled bronze axes and short spears, and the largest body of all, Egyptian archers, deployed on the wings and at the head of the column, together with several hundred two-wheeled chariots formed into a strike group with a driver and an archer in each car. Behind them came ox-carts and donkey and mule trains carrying rations, while Egyptian scribes wrote down the day's camp and the towns passed through. The opposing coalition was the Hurrian kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia, whose ruler called himself the Great King and exercised suzerainty over the Syrian states - Qatna, Tunip, Aleppo, Byblos and Sidon - together with Carchemish and Emar on the middle Euphrates, and he drew in the sand-dwelling nomads of the Orontes valley. The coalition fielded infantry, chariotry and Hurrian archers, supplemented by irregular auxiliaries raised by the individual city states. The Hittites still held the Anatolian plateau and Babylonia still controlled the sources of lapis lazuli and tin; neither fought here, yet both decided where the war's material resources came from.
people: 核心人物是埃及法老圖特摩斯三世（Menkheperre）。他在哈特謝普蘇特治下以少年之身即位，成年後親掌兵權，這一次遠征正是他統治中期用來餵養戰功集團、鞏固王位的老手段；國王本人統率大軍，後方日常指揮由宰相與弓箭手隊長一類的軍職分擔。對面的「大王」是胡里王室的君主，此人的名號在文獻中多有出入，而與他通信、聞名於世的圖胥拉塔屬於稍後一代；卡爾凱美什與阿勒頗一系的諸王在年表中只以「某某之王」出現，名字能否對應同一個人，歷來有爭議。第五次遠征中的敘利亞領袖，多數只有城邦之名而無個人之名，也沒有留下自己的記錄。唯一以自己的聲音說話的，是後來阿瑪納字母裡米坦尼求援與討價還價的書信，那些文字讓「大王」的處境第一次以當事人的說法流傳下來，也讓後人看出聯盟內部的裂痕：北方各邦未必真心服從大王的號令，埃及正是從這道縫裡切了進去。
peopleEn: The central figure is the Egyptian pharaoh Thutmose III (Menkheperre). He had taken the throne as a boy under the regency of Hatshepsut and had taken power into his own hands as a man, and this expedition was one of the old devices by which he in the middle of his reign fed a body of men whose standing depended on war and confirmed his own kingship; the king led the army in person, while day-to-day command at the rear fell to the vizier and to officers of the kind of the chief of the bowmen. Opposite him stood the Great King, ruler of the Hurrian house; his name is given differently from document to document, and Tushratta, the best-known ruler through the surviving correspondence, belongs to a slightly later generation. The kings of Carchemish and of Aleppo appear in the annals only as the king of such-and-such, and whether such a title refers to the same individual from one year to the next remains disputed. Most of the Syrian leaders of the fifth campaign are known only by the name of their city, not by their own names, and none of them left a record in his own voice. The only man who does speak for the Great King is heard much later, in the Amarna letters, where Mitanni begs, bargains and complains; those texts show the Great King's predicament for the first time in his own words, and they also expose the cracks inside the coalition, for the northern states did not necessarily obey the Great King wholeheartedly, and that was the seam Egypt worked its way into.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及月牙劍：內彎的單刃青銅短劍，形制源於中期王朝的鵝嘴斧，第二中間期已見於實戰裝備，新王國初期是埃及近戰步兵的標準配備。刃口向內彎，砍入甲胄或人體後不必把劍拔出，可連砍帶拉地撕開傷口，故有「砍下去不用拔」之說；它配小型圓盾與直刃短匕，專門對付失去衝力的散兵。劍身為銅或青銅，比後來的直刃劍短而重，穿透鱗甲的能力有限，遇重甲只能砍、拖、擲，因此埃及步兵近戰仍以長柄銅斧與標槍為主，弓手才是全軍人數最多的一環：角、筋、木製的複合弓，箭簇以燙硬打製。車兵是突破與追擊的力量，木輪雙輪車自圖特摩斯三世起四匹馬挽者漸多；攻城時備有攻城塔、撞錘與填土斜坡，並以雲梯攀城，攻堅前先以弓手與標槍清理城頭。守方與聯軍同樣以複合弓遠射，近戰用銅斧與雙刃斧。補給靠驢騾隊與牛車運糧，以及城邦徵發的穀物、葡萄酒與金屬；銅來自西奈，錫與青金石經巴比倫方向運來，黎巴嫩雪松木則年年由海路運往下埃及。須留意的是，第十八王朝中葉之後月牙形劍在軍陣中已逐漸退場，銅斧與直刃青銅劍才是常備，畫面中仍留下月牙弧刃，多是儀式與象徵的沿用。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian khopesh: a short bronze sword with a single edge and a back curved forward, a form derived from the Middle Kingdom duckbill axe, already in service in the Second Intermediate Period and standard issue for Egyptian close combat infantry at the start of the New Kingdom. Because the edge turns inward, the blade can be drawn through a wound instead of being pulled back out, which is what the phrase 'cut and never withdraw' refers to; it was carried with a small round shield and a straight-edged dagger, and was used against troops who had lost their momentum. Its body is copper or bronze, shorter and heavier than the later straight swords, and poor at piercing scale armour; against heavy protection it could only chop, tear and throw. Egyptian close combat therefore leaned on the long-handled bronze axe and the javelin, and it was the archer who made up the largest single body of the army: composite bows of horn, sinew and wood, with hardened arrowheads. Chariotry supplied the breakthrough and the pursuit, and from the reign of Thutmose III four-horse teams became more common; for siege work the Egyptians had towers, rams and earthen ramps, and scaled walls with ladders after archers and javelins had cleared the parapet. The defence used the same composite bow and fought close with bronze and double-bit axes. Supply depended on donkey and mule trains and ox-carts for grain, together with grain, wine and metal requisitioned from the towns; copper came from Sinai, tin and lapis lazuli from the Babylonian direction, and cedar from Lebanon came down the coast year by year. One point should be kept in view: through the middle of the Eighteenth Dynasty the khopesh was already fading out of the battle line, and straight bronze swords and crescent-bladed axes became the standing equipment, so that the curved blade surviving in the art is a survival of ceremony and symbol as much as of use.
tactics: 埃及遠征有一套固定章法。軍隊不整隊行軍，而分數路縱隊同時推進：中央縱隊沿大道走，左翼沿奧龍特斯河谷作先鋒，右翼貼近海岸與山麓作掩護，三路在預定會合處一齊壓上；沿途每日宿營前派出偵察，軍中文書把道路、村落與渡口記在行程表上，殘存的地名表便是後人還原路線的依據。渡河是全戰最要緊的一步：河上無橋，須以船、筏或浮橋分批渡過，埃及人甚至先造好船、由海路運至陸路再搬過陸地，渡口一旦被守，遠征即告中止；渡河之後大軍立刻圍城或設營，把城內的水井與耕地控制在自己手裡。會戰陣形以步兵正面與弓手在兩翼展開，戰車不置於前線，待敵陣出現缺口時一齊投入，衝開之後才讓步兵帶月牙劍湧入缺口作近身砍殺。攻城多圍而不打與突擊並用：先以弓手與標槍清理城頭，再以雲梯攀城或斷糧迫降，必要時堆土築斜坡，把車兵送上城牆高度。年表中記載過一次對奧龍特斯河畔沙丘民族城邑的圍攻，法老下令沿山壁掘進隧道、引水灌入，屬於十八王朝攻城術中最具體的一次記載。外交與戰爭並行：對敘利亞城邦用「宗主—納貢」收編，對「大王」則以軍威迫其送來黃金與青金石。
tacticsEn: Egyptian expeditions followed a fixed routine. The army did not march as one column but advanced in several columns at once: the central column on the main road, the left wing ahead along the Orontes valley, the right wing close to the coast and the foothills for cover, the three pressing on together at a fixed point of rendezvous. Scouting parties went out before the daily camp was pitched, and the scribes wrote down roads, villages and fords on the itinerary, and the surviving lists of place names are what allow the route to be reconstructed. Crossing the rivers was the most critical step of all: there were no bridges, so troops had to be ferried by boat, raft or pontoon, and the Egyptians even built their boats in the north, carried them by sea and hauled them overland; once a crossing was held by the enemy the expedition was over. After crossing, the army at once invested the town or set up camp, taking control of the wells and the farmland inside it. In battle the infantry formed the front with the archers extended on the wings; the chariots were not put in the line but held back, to be thrown in together when the enemy line opened, and only then did the infantry with their khopeshes pour into the gap for hand-to-hand work. Sieges combined blockade with assault: archers and javelins cleared the walls, ladders were brought up, or the town was starved into surrender, and where necessary earthen ramps were built to bring the chariots up to the height of the wall. The annals record one siege of a town of the sand-dwellers on the Orontes in which the pharaoh ordered a tunnel driven into the hillside and water let in through it, the most concrete piece of Eighteenth Dynasty siegecraft we have. Diplomacy ran alongside the war: the Syrian states were taken in as tributaries, while the Great King was pressed, by military demonstration, to send gold and lapis lazuli.
data: 可核對的數字如下。年代通常記作前1450年，屬於圖特摩斯三世統治中段那幾次北征之一，不同編年體系另有前1457年、前1446年等說法；他的傳統在位年數約五十年，統治期約自前1480年至前1425年，其間頭三十年幾乎年年北征。遠征次數有兩套：曼涅托把它記作十七次，後世學者通常整理為十六次敘利亞戰役外加一次努比亞遠征，編號因此在不同版本中前後錯開一格。距離方面，隊伍自三角洲的孟斐斯基地北行至奧龍特斯河谷，約一千至一千二百公里；奧龍特斯河在敘利亞境內的可航段約三百五十公里，由比布魯斯到阿勒頗約二百五十公里，阿勒頗到幼發拉底河畔的卡爾凱美什不足一百公里；一日行程一般二十至三十公里，單程行軍就要三十日以上。兵力方面，埃及核心步兵一般估計在數千至一萬之間，其中弓手占多數，戰車常在數百輛的量級，部分估算高至數千輛；聯軍靠各城邦拼湊，總數亦在數千至一萬上下，車兵比例低於埃及。物資來源同樣可查：埃及從西奈的塞伊納等銅礦取銅，從巴比倫方向取得青金石，銅與青金石多經米坦尼一線轉運，這說明商路正是爭端所在。戰果數字須打折扣：埃及碑文以擄獲人數、馬匹與金銀器計功，數量常被後世學者下修數倍，宜視為宣傳量度而非統計。最硬的旁證是阿瑪納字母：現存約三百五十封，其中逾二百封涉及米坦尼。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are these. The date is usually given as 1450 BC, one of the northern expeditions of the middle of Thutmose III's reign, though other chronologies give 1457 BC or 1446 BC; his traditional reign of about fifty years runs from roughly 1480 to 1425 BC, and for the first thirty years of it he campaigned in the north almost annually. The number of campaigns comes in two versions: Manetho counts seventeen, and modern scholars usually sort them into sixteen Syrian campaigns plus one Nubian expedition, so that the numbering slips by one between editions. As for distance, the column travelled about 1,000 to 1,200 km from its base at Memphis in the Delta up to the Orontes valley; about 350 km of the Orontes lie within Syria, Byblos to Aleppo is roughly 250 km, and Aleppo to Carchemish on the Euphrates is under 100 km. At a day's march of 20 to 30 km, the outward march alone took more than thirty days. On strength, the Egyptian infantry is generally estimated at several thousand to ten thousand men, archers forming the greater part of it, with chariots in the hundreds and some estimates running to thousands; the coalition was patched together by the city states and was of the same order, with a lower proportion of chariots. The sources of material are equally traceable: Egypt took copper from Sinai and lapis lazuli from the Babylonian direction, and both moved along the Mitanni line, which shows that the caravan road was what the quarrel was about. Figures for results must be discounted: Egyptian monuments reckon spoil in captives, horses and plate, and later scholars routinely reduce them severalfold, so they are best read as propaganda rather than statistics. The hardest evidence of all is the Amarna archive, of which about 350 letters survive, over two hundred of them concerning Mitanni.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是地理與商路：埃及要保住從西奈運出的銅礦、從黎巴嫩運入的雪松木，以及由巴比倫方向經米坦尼轉入的青金石，這條商路一旦被截斷，新王國的財政與神廟工程都要停滯；更關鍵的是幼發拉底河中游的卡爾凱美什與埃馬爾控制了自上游運銅、鉛、錫下行的通道，誰占住那兩城，誰就捏住幼發拉底河兩岸的關稅與人頭稅。中層是宗主權之爭：米坦尼大王在西屬的敘利亞諸邦面前自居宗主，埃及則要否認這層宗主關係，寧可自己收編卡脫納、圖尼普與阿勒頗。最內層是政治與戰功：圖特摩斯三世成年後需要北方戰功來鞏固王位與一批有戰功的將領，敘利亞戰事既能收回邊境要塞，也能餵養軍功集團。第五次遠征的直接起因，在流傳的年表裡只剩斷簡：可以確定的是聯盟不肯照舊納貢，奧龍特斯河谷的邊境站與商隊屢遭襲擾，大王的軍隊在北部集結，埃及遂再度揮師北上，把一次邊界衝突擴成深入幼發拉底河上游的遠征。
causeEn: There are three layers of reason behind the fighting. The outermost is geography and trade: Egypt needed the copper from Sinai, the cedar from Lebanon and the lapis lazuli that reached it from Babylonia through Mitanni, and if that road were cut the finances and the temple building of the New Kingdom would stall. More pointedly, Carchemish and Emar on the middle Euphrates controlled the movement of copper, lead and tin coming down from the upper river, and whoever held those two towns held the tolls and the head taxes of both banks of the Euphrates. The middle layer is a dispute over overlordship: the Great King of Mitanni presented himself to his western subjects in Syria as their overlord, while Egypt denied that relationship and preferred to take Qatna, Tunip and Aleppo into her own network. The innermost layer is political: as a grown man Thutmose III needed northern victories to confirm his kingship and to keep a company of generals and officials rewarded, and a Syrian war both recovered frontier strongholds and fed that company. The immediate occasion of the fifth expedition survives only in broken fragments; what is certain is that the coalition would not pay the customary tribute, that frontier stations and caravans in the Orontes valley were repeatedly attacked, that the Great King was concentrating troops in the north, and that Egypt marched north again, turning a border clash into an expedition deep up the Euphrates.
impact: 對埃及，這場戰役是亞洲政策連續推進的一環，第五次遠征之後，敘利亞自此更形深入埃及的宗主體系：卡脫納、圖尼普、比布魯斯、西頓與阿勒頗按年進貢金、銀、鉛、錫、銅、象牙、馬匹、葡萄酒、食用油與人丁，埃及在本地設官徵收，敘利亞的葡萄酒與黎巴嫩雪松大量運入三角洲，神廟與船塢的建材因此不斷。對米坦尼，這是一場結構性挫敗：大王的西屬地盤被逐出幼發拉底河以西，王室退守上美索不達米亞，往後數十年只能靠外交求生。更遠地看，這條路也通向後來兩大強權在幼發拉底河上游的角力：前1400年代赫梯自安納托利亞南下，前13世紀埃及拉美西斯二世與赫梯王穆瓦塔里二世在卡爾凱美什會戰，讓這座城再次成為前線；而阿瑪納字母因記錄了米坦尼的求饒與兩國彼此試探，也成了後世重建青銅時代國際外交的第一手材料。對武器史而言，這一役則是月牙形銅劍退場的分水嶺：第十八王朝中期之後，埃及軍陣的近戰主力由月牙劍改為直刃青銅劍與月牙刃銅斧，象徵意味在剩下的戰役裡逐漸壓過實戰功能。
impactEn: For Egypt, this campaign was one of a continuous series carrying the Asian policy forward, and after the fifth expedition Syria lay more deeply inside the Egyptian tributary system: Qatna, Tunip, Byblos, Sidon and Aleppo paid yearly tribute in gold, silver, lead, tin, copper, ivory, horses, wine, oil and people, Egyptian officials were appointed to collect it, and the wine of Syria and the cedar of Lebanon came down to the Delta in bulk, keeping the temples and the shipyards supplied. For Mitanni it was a structural defeat: the Great King's western lands were pushed out beyond the Euphrates, the royal house withdrew to Upper Mesopotamia, and for decades afterwards it survived by diplomacy. Further out, the same road leads to the later rivalry of the two great powers on the upper Euphrates: in the 1400s BC the Hittites came down from Anatolia, and in the 13th century BC Ramesses II of Egypt met Muttattalli II of the Hittites at Carchemish, and that city was once more a front line. The Amarna letters, recording Mitanni's entreaties and the mutual probing of the two courts, are the first-hand material from which the international diplomacy of the Bronze Age has been reconstructed. For the history of arms, this campaign is a watershed in the retreat of the crescent-bladed bronze sword: after the middle of the Eighteenth Dynasty the close-combat mainstay of the Egyptian army was the straight bronze sword and the crescent-bladed axe, and in the campaigns that remained the symbolic use of the old blade gradually outweighed its working use.
result: 結果是埃及以野戰勝利換來政治上限：聯盟在奧龍特斯河與幼發拉底河上游的抵抗被壓下去，卡爾凱美什一線再度落入埃及的進攻範圍，大王一方雖未覆亡，仍保有「大王」名號與上美索不達米亞的核心地盤，只好加大歲貢、加快納貢頻率，以保住殘餘的宗主虛名。若要說勝負怎樣算，埃及贏了戰役卻沒有贏下北界：它無法在幼發拉底河以北常駐軍隊，影響仍要靠一次次重兵出動維持，編年上的編號也說明遠征遠未結束——這場戰役之後，仍有十一次敘利亞戰役排在其後，直到後段那些小規模掠奪式的出兵。今天能確認的細節有限：第五次遠征的過程多靠卡納克年表的殘片、軍隊地名表與被征服城鎮的名單拼回，月牙劍手的近身格鬥、弓手在會戰兩翼的箭雨、渡河之後的圍城與掘進隧道，是這場戰爭留給後世最清晰的畫面。
resultEn: The outcome was that Egypt bought political parity with a field victory: the resistance of the coalition along the Orontes and the upper Euphrates was put down, Carchemish and its line fell again within Egypt's reach, and although the Great King was not destroyed he kept his title and his core territory in Upper Mesopotamia and had to increase his tribute and the frequency of his payments in order to preserve the appearance of overlordship. Judged as a contest, Egypt won the campaign but not the northern frontier: it could not keep a standing army beyond the Euphrates, and the arrangement had to be maintained by repeated expeditions - which the numbering itself shows, since eleven more Syrian campaigns follow this one, down to the small raiding expeditions of the later years. What can be confirmed today is limited: the course of the fifth expedition has to be pieced together from the fragments of the Karnak annals, the lists of place names and the enumerations of towns taken, and the clearest picture it leaves is of khopesh men fighting hand to hand, of arrow-falls from the wings, of the sieges that followed the crossings and of tunnels driven into a hillside. The record of this war is thin, and it is the annalistic fragments rather than any continuous narrative that has to carry it.
